status: Attribution complete. No new production candidate or speed acceptance.

failedCapture.interpretation: Both ten-second stack-plus-invalidation captures filled their buffers. Their partial data is preserved and excluded. Calibration passed, but neither dense case has verified ordered updates in that failed report.

calibration.lineAndColumnConversion: Trace call-site lines and columns are one-based. Source-map lines are one-based; columns are zero-based UTF-16.

limits: Intrusive three-second captures within ten-second quiet streams. No paired speed acceptance, native-v2 equivalence, field INP, M2 Air, battery or heap-leak conclusion.
Call stacks identify binding call sites that trigger observed style/layout work. They do not prove all work is avoidable or that removing a reader removes the underlying layout.
Wall intervals are clipped to the marker window. Per-category unions avoid double counting within a category; different categories and inclusive stacks can overlap and must not be summed.
Both 300-update streams are verified after the capture windows. This does not prove all updates rendered within those windows.
The earlier stack-plus-invalidation capture filled the trace buffer in both cases. Its partial data remains preserved and is excluded from this analysis.
CPU profile sample weights are not used.

sourceMapBuildReceipt.scope: For mapping forced layout binding call-site stacks. This is not a timing run or an optimization.

recordedTaskBusyAudit.scope: Both arms of the complete rejected shared-scroll six-pair comparison. Baseline 9e20; candidate 59e1. This is not a new speed result for delivered b7c3.
recordedTaskBusyAudit.interpretation: Every recorded normal-streaming window is close to fully occupied on the renderer task clock (98.06% to 98.68%). A fixed window can conceal a smaller per-update work reduction while the renderer remains busy. Independent response-time and completion/throughput evidence is needed. This does not establish any rejected candidate as faster or change the 20% target.
recordedTaskBusyAudit.limits: TaskDuration is renderer task duration, not whole-machine CPU use. This audit uses existing complete Linux software-rendering captures and has no M2 Air conclusion.

interpretation: The positive control produces 22 stack-bearing style/layout records at the known geometry-read call site. The negative textContent control produces none. Trace call-site coordinates are calibrated as one-based lines and columns; source-map columns are zero-based UTF-16.

In the no-selection capture, selection.rangeCount triggers 76 observed style events and 72 layout events. The generic saved-scrollTop read triggers another 36 style and 31 layout events. The motion target calculation triggers four of each.

In the focused-composer capture, the selection getter no longer appears as a forced layout call site. All 47 observed layout records have no JavaScript stack, while style work also shifts toward frame processing. This is a diagnostic control, not a paired speed comparison.
Removing one getter can move work to another binding read or to frame processing. These call-site records do not establish how much work a production change would remove.

The full existing reference run is close to fully occupied during all twelve normal-streaming windows. Keep the independent latency, native-input and correctness controls. Do not use the task-busy cap to accept rejected candidates.
limits: Stack capture and CPU profiling change scheduling. No timing comparison, native-v2 equivalence, field INP, M2 Air, battery or memory-leak claim follows.
Per-category wall unions are clipped to the markers. Different categories and inclusive stacks overlap and must not be summed. Durations include instrumentation effects.
All 600 updates are verified after the trace windows. This does not prove all of them rendered within those windows.
The main reference comparison quoted for the task-busy audit is the existing rejected shared-scroll run. Its assets differ from the delivered b7c3 build.
No production source, native interaction policy or benchmark deadline changes are retained. All temporary browser sources are removed.
The 20% normal-streaming target and original-baseline final matrix remain open.
